```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, forcats
library(sf)          # simple features: spatial data as a data frame
library(tigris)      # downloads Census TIGER/Line boundary files

# Cache the downloaded boundaries so tigris doesn't re-download every knit
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
```

## Step 1 — Read the data

```{r read}
homicides <- read_csv("../data/homicide-data.csv")

dim(homicides)   # 52179 rows x 12 columns
```
## Step 2 - Filter for Denver and build two grouping variables
## Keep 3 most common race groups in Denver and put everything else into a single category

```{r denver}
denver <- homicides %>%
  filter(city == "Denver") %>%
  mutate(
    lat = as.numeric(lat),
    lon = as.numeric(lon),
    solved = if_else(disposition == "Closed by arrest", "Solved", "Unsolved"),
    solved = factor(solved, levels = c("Solved", "Unsolved")),
    victim_race = fct_lump_n(
      factor(victim_race),
      n = 3,
      other_level = "All other races"
    ),
    victim_race = fct_infreq(victim_race)          # order legend by frequency
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon))

count(denver, solved)
count(denver, victim_race)
```
## Step 3 Turn points into sf object

```{r points}
denver_sf <- st_as_sf(denver, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

denver_sf
```

## Step 4 Download tract boundaries with tigris

```{r tracts, results = "hide"}
denver_tracts <- tracts(
  state  = "CO",
  county = "Denver",
  cb     = TRUE,
  year   = 2020
)
```

## Step 5 Put both layers (sf from 3 and tracts from 4) in same coordinate system. Transform points into polygons CRS.

```{r crs}
st_crs(denver_tracts)$epsg   # 4269
st_crs(denver_sf)$epsg       # 4326

denver_sf <- st_transform(denver_sf, st_crs(denver_tracts))
```
## Step 6 Build map

```{r map, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
race_colors <- c(
  "Black"           = "#0072B2",
  "White"           = "#D55E00",
  "Hispanic"        = "#009E73",
  "All other races" = "#9467BD"
)

denver_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data      = denver_tracts,
    fill      = "grey96",
    color     = "grey97",
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = denver_sf,
    aes(color = victim_race),
    size  = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ solved) +
  scale_color_manual(values = race_colors, name = "Victim race") +
  labs(
    title    = "Homicides in Denver, Colorado, 2010-2017",
    subtitle = "Solved (closed by arrest) versus unsolved, by victim race",
    caption  = paste(
      "Source: Washington Post homicide database.",
      "Tract boundaries: US Census Bureau via tigris."
    )
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12,
                                   margin = margin(b = 6))
  )

denver_map
```
